issues.sym: The oil pressure light comes on, the engine knocks, stalls or loses power, and in the worst cases the engine seizes. Owners report repair bills of several thousand dollars.
issues.why: Long factory oil-change intervals on conventional oil let sludge and carbon build up and block the oil pickup screen in the pan, starving the engine of oil. Saab extended engine coverage at the time; that coverage has long ended.
issues.next: If you see the oil light, stop and shut the engine off. On a car with an unknown history, have the oil pan removed and the pickup cleaned, update the crankcase ventilation, and change synthetic oil about every 5,000 miles.

issues.sym: The engine misfires, runs rough, flashes the check engine light, stalls while driving, or cranks but won't start.
issues.why: The direct ignition (DI) cassette, which sits on top of the spark plugs and replaces separate coils, fails with age and heat.
issues.next: Have the misfire codes read. Replacing the DI cassette, usually with new spark plugs, is the common fix.

issues.t: Ignition module can overheat and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine misfires or stalls while driving.
issues.why: A transistor in the ignition discharge module can overheat and burn out. Saab recalled modules built before a production change on the 2.3L four-cylinder and 3.0L V6.
issues.next: Ask a dealer or Saab specialist to check the module and the recall status.

issues.t: Oil leaks from excess crankcase pressure
issues.sym: Oil leaks from the timing cover, valve cover or rear main seal, oily engine, burning oil smell.
issues.why: When the crankcase ventilation clogs, pressure builds inside the engine and pushes oil past gaskets and seals.
issues.next: Fix the ventilation system first, then repair the leaking gaskets. Otherwise new seals will leak again.

issues.t: PCV check valve and hose failure
issues.sym: Blue smoke at start-up, oil leaks, rough idle or a check engine light.
issues.why: The crankcase ventilation check valves and hoses crack or break. Saab released an updated crankcase vent kit.
issues.next: Ask a shop to install the latest version of the ventilation kit. It is inexpensive compared with the damage sludge causes.

issues.t: Coolant bypass valve cracking and dumping coolant
issues.sym: A sudden coolant leak under the car, the low-coolant warning, steam, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: A plastic coolant bypass valve in the heater hoses cracks with age and can lose coolant quickly.
issues.next: Stop if the engine overheats. The valve itself is inexpensive; many owners replace it before it fails.

issues.t: Turbocharger seal failure and blue smoke
issues.sym: Blue smoke at cold start, oil use, loss of power or a whining turbo.
issues.why: Turbo seals wear out, especially when oil changes were stretched or the oil was sludged.
issues.next: Check the oil level often and have the turbo inspected. Check oil feed lines and ventilation before installing a new turbo.

issues.sym: The engine dies on the road or won't start, often needing a tow.
issues.why: The in-tank fuel pump wears out.
issues.next: Have fuel pressure tested to confirm the pump before replacing it.

issues.sym: Clunking when shifting or accelerating, lurching, and extra vibration.
issues.why: The rubber engine and transmission mounts sag and crack with age.
issues.next: Have all mounts checked together; often more than one is worn.

issues.sym: The temperature gauge stays low, the heater is weak, and a check engine light may come on.
issues.why: The thermostat sticks open so the engine never warms up fully.
issues.next: Replace the thermostat. A genuine or OEM-quality part lasts longer.

issues.t: Throttle body failure and limp mode
issues.sym: A check engine light such as P1230, sudden loss of power, or the engine dying at speed.
issues.why: The electronic throttle body fails.
issues.next: Have the codes read. A rebuilt or new throttle body is the usual repair.

issues.sym: The engine stalls or won't start, sometimes after warming up.
issues.why: The crankshaft position sensor, which tells the computer engine speed, fails.
issues.next: A shop can confirm with codes and a live data check. The sensor is a modest repair.

issues.sym: A rattle from the front of the engine, especially at start-up.
issues.why: Worn chains, guides and tensioners, often linked to sludge. Saab issued a bulletin on timing chain noise and sludge.
issues.next: Have it inspected promptly. Chain failure can wreck the engine.

issues.sym: Lines or letters missing on the dash display.
issues.why: The LCD in the Saab Information Display wears out.
issues.next: Only the LCD needs replacing; specialists and DIY kits cover it.

issues.t: Wipers, turn signals and windows stop working
issues.sym: The wipers, turn signals and power windows all stop working at once.
issues.why: A Saab bulletin covers an electrical fault that knocks out these circuits on 1999-2009 cars.
issues.next: Have a Saab specialist check the bulletin. Don't drive in rain without wipers.

issues.sym: One or more doors won't lock or unlock with the key fob or switch.
issues.why: A Saab bulletin covers inoperative door locks.
issues.next: Have the lock motor and wiring checked.

issues.t: Wheel bolts can break after rust on the hub
issues.sym: Wheel bolts loosen or break; a wobble or clunk from a wheel.
issues.why: Switching between alloy and steel wheels can let rust build on the hub face, which fatigues the wheel bolts. Saab warned that a safety defect may exist.
issues.next: Clean the hub faces whenever wheels are swapped, and torque the bolts correctly.

issues.t: A-pillar trim may not protect in a crash (recall)
issues.sym: No warning sign.
issues.why: The upper interior trim didn't meet a federal head-impact standard. Saab installed improved A-pillar trim.
issues.next: Check with a GM dealer that the recall was done.

issues.sym: No warning sign; the danger is metal fragments in a crash.
issues.why: The driver frontal airbag inflator can rupture from excess pressure.
issues.next: Check your VIN on NHTSA's site and have the free replacement done.

issues.t: Tail light or turn signal malfunction
issues.sym: A tail light or rear turn signal stops working, or a bulb warning appears.
issues.why: Owners report rear lighting faults on the new 2011 model; the exterior lighting is the most-complained area.
issues.next: Have the bulb, socket and wiring checked first. Fix it quickly, since drivers behind you rely on these lights.

issues.sym: A headlight warning, or the headlights aim too high or low.
issues.why: The automatic headlight leveling system, which keeps the beams aimed as the car's load changes, develops a fault. Owners report repair bills around $800.
issues.next: Have the leveling sensor and headlight motor diagnosed. Badly aimed lights can dazzle other drivers or cut your own view.

issues.sym: The brake pedal stays down or feels sticky.
issues.why: Owners of the 2011 model report the brake pedal sticking. The exact cause isn't documented, so the pedal assembly, booster and brake light switch area all need checking.
issues.next: Treat any brake pedal problem as urgent. Have the brakes inspected before driving further.

issues.sym: The car is dead after sitting; no crank, no start.
issues.why: An electronic module stays awake after the car is locked and slowly drains the battery. GM issued several bulletins on this for the 2011 9-5.
issues.next: If the battery tests good but keeps going flat, ask a shop for a parasitic draw test to find the circuit that stays on.

issues.t: ABS warning light from wheel speed sensor
issues.sym: The ABS warning light comes on.
issues.why: A fault with the wheel speed sensors turns on the ABS light. GM issued a bulletin on it.
issues.next: Normal brakes still work, but ABS and stability control may be off. Have the codes read to find which sensor is at fault.

issues.sym: The sunroof binds, is noisy, reverses or leaks.
issues.why: The sunroof mechanism binds or its drains clog, which GM covers in a bulletin on noisy, binding or leaking sunroofs.
issues.next: Clear the drain tubes and have the track and glass adjusted. Water inside the car can damage wiring and cause mold.
